movement_source: row 'Net interest margin (%)', column 30 Jun 20 (Full Year Ended) -> column 30 Jun 21 (Full Year Ended)
headline: CBA's Group net interest margin fell 4 basis points in FY21 to 2.03%, from 2.07% in FY20, on a cash, continuing-operations basis (ev-18, ev-1, ev-16). Net interest income still rose $229 million or 1% to $18,839 million, because a $32 billion or 4% increase in average interest earning assets to $930 billion more than offset the margin decline (ev-2). The whole of the decline is explained by balance-sheet liquidity: higher liquids cost 4 bpts, which CBA says had "Minimal impact on NII" (ev-14), leaving the margin "Flat ex liquids – pressure from lower interest rates, offset by favourable portfolio mix, lower wholesale funding costs" (ev-13). Within the rest, asset pricing (-2), deposit pricing and funding (-3) and capital and other (-2) were offset by portfolio mix (+2), basis risk incl. replicating portfolio (+3) and Treasury & Markets (+2) (ev-12). On an including-discontinued-operations basis the same row prints 2.03% vs 2.08%, a 5 bpt fall (ev-19).

drivers.narrative: "Decreased margin by 4 basis points driven by increased lower yielding non-lending interest earning assets, including liquid assets" — non-lending IEA rose $20bn or 12% to $195bn, including a $17bn rise in average liquid assets on strong customer deposit growth. CBA flags "Minimal impact on NII".

Lower business lending margins (down 1 bpt) from "repricing actions to support businesses during COVID-19", and lower consumer finance margins (down 1 bpt) from fewer interest earning credit card balances. Home lending margins were flat: repricing +9 bpts, offset by switching from variable to fixed (-5 bpts) and increased competition (-4 bpts).

Lower earnings on transaction and savings deposits "mainly due to decreases in the cash rate" (down 7 bpts), partly offset by higher benefits from the replicating portfolio (up 2 bpts) and lower wholesale funding costs (up 2 bpts).

Lower earnings on Group capital "due to the falling interest rate environment" (down 3 bpts), partly offset by increased contribution from New Zealand (up 1 bpt) reflecting lower wholesale funding costs and favourable portfolio mix, itself partly offset by RBNZ cash rate cuts.

Higher average deposit funding ratio (Jun 21: 77%; Jun 20: 71%) from strong transaction and savings deposit growth, customers switching to at-call deposits and the drawdown of the TFF (up 4 bpts), partly offset by unfavourable asset mix (down 2 bpts) from declining higher-margin consumer finance balances.

Basis risk is the spread between the 3 month bank bill swap rate and the 3 month overnight index swap rate. Margin rose 3 bpts on "a decrease in the average spread notwithstanding a structural reduction in exposure" from growth in cash-rate-linked deposits and a mix shift to fixed rate home loans.
"Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by higher bonds and commodities financing income in Global Markets" — consistent with the $3bn rise in average trading assets in Global Markets.

disagreements.topic: FY21 vs FY20 Group NIM movement: continuing operations vs including discontinued operations
disagreements.explanation: The FY21 KPI table prints the NIM row twice. The continuing-operations block is CBA's headline framing, matches the Group NII/NIM analysis table and the FY20 book's own 2.07% comparative, and is the basis of the published seven-bar walk. The including-discontinued row differs only in the FY20 base (2.08%).

limitations: The results book publishes its FY20->FY21 decomposition as narrative paragraphs rather than as a chart; the seven quantified bars were corroborated by the results presentation p63 waterfall (FY20 207 -> FY21 203), which passed the sum check and matched the book bar-for-bar, so no framing conflict arose.

CBA qualifies the -4 bpt liquids bar as having 'Minimal impact on NII': the margin dilution is largely mechanical denominator growth from a $17bn rise in average liquid assets, not an earnings loss, and CBA describes the margin as 'Flat ex liquids'. Read the headline -4 bpts with that qualification.

The +3 bpt basis risk bar is labelled 'Basis Risk (incl RP)' on the slide, so it may bundle replicating-portfolio effects; the book separately reports a +2 bpt replicating portfolio benefit inside the funding costs bar, and CBA does not reconcile these labels.

Sub-part figures inside each driver (e.g. home loan repricing +9 bpts, deposit cash-rate impact -7 bpts) are stated only in the FY21 documents; they are not independently corroborated in the FY20 book.

evidence_records.quote: Net interest margin (%) 2. 03 2. 07 (4)bpts 2. 04 2. 01 3 bpts

Net interest income was $18,839 million, an increase of $229 million or 1% on the prior year. The result was driven by a $32 billion or 4% increase in average interest earning assets to $930 billion, partly offset by a 4 basis point decrease in net interest margin to 2.03%.
Liquid assets: Decreased margin by 4 basis points driven by increased lower yielding non-lending interest earning assets, including liquid assets.

Asset pricing: Decreased margin by 2 basis points driven by lower business lending margins (down 1 basis point) from repricing actions to support businesses during COVID-19, and lower consumer finance margins (down 1 basis point) from a reduction in the proportion of interest earning credit card balances.

Home lending margins were flat, reflecting repricing (up 9 basis points), offset by the impact of customers switching from higher margin loans to lower margin loans, particularly from variable rate to fixed rate loans (down 5 basis points) and increased competition (down 4 basis points).

Funding costs: Decreased margin by 3 basis points, reflecting lower earnings on transaction and savings deposits mainly due to decreases in the cash rate (down 7 basis points), partly offset by higher benefits from the replicating portfolio (up 2 basis points) and lower wholesale funding costs (up 2 basis points).

Non-lending interest earning asset average balances increased $20 billion or 12% on the prior year to $195 billion, driven by a $17 billion increase in average liquid asset balances mainly due to strong customer deposit growth

Portfolio mix: Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by a higher average deposit funding ratio (30 June 2021: 77%; 30 June 2020: 71%) due to strong growth in transaction and savings deposits, customers switching to at-call deposits, and the drawdown of the TFF (up 4 basis points), partly offset by an unfavourable impact from asset mix (down 2 basis points), mainly due to a decline in higher margin consumer finance balances.

The Bank's margin increased 3 basis points reflecting a decrease in the average spread notwithstanding a structural reduction in exposure to basis risk due to strong growth in cash rate linked deposits and a mix shift towards fixed rate home loans.

Capital and other: Decreased margin by 2 basis points driven by lower earnings on Group capital due to the falling interest rate environment (down 3 basis points), partly offset by increased contribution from New Zealand (up 1 basis point), reflecting lower wholesale funding costs and favourable portfolio mix, partly offset by the impact from RBNZ cash rate cuts.
Treasury and Markets: Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by higher bonds and commodities financing income in Global Markets.
